Disposable income is the money households have to spend or save after income tax and social contributions, including social welfare payments. In 2024, disposable income per person was highest in Dublin, at €33,889, and lowest in Longford, at €23,725. The figures are not adjusted for differences between counties in the cost of living, such as housing costs.

{{< chart economy-income-map >}}

## Poverty and social exclusion

In 2025, 18.8% of people in Ireland were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, as Eurostat defines it, compared with 20.9% across the EU. Ireland's rate was close to the middle of the 27 EU countries.

{{< chart economy-poverty-eu >}}

## Ireland and Northern Ireland

The CSO and NISRA publish household income for Ireland and Northern Ireland on the same basis, adjusted for the different price levels. In 2023, disposable household income per person was 13% higher in Ireland than in Northern Ireland.
